scopeBoundary: Controlled local production-preview evidence only; hosted and physical-device validation is reserved for Prompt 10.

environment.topology: Vite production preview and Flask on dynamic loopback ports with a disposable SQLite database
environment.sampling: Five cold or cache-controlled serial runs in a fresh browser context
environment.percentileMethod: Nearest-rank p95; with five samples this is the maximum
metricSources: PerformanceObserver layout-shift entries using the standard 1-second-gap/5-second CLS session-window algorithm
PerformanceObserver longtask entries with preserved browser attribution
Chrome trace and CPU-profile diagnosis for the baseline long task

layoutShift.primarySource: .gv-footer moving after the undersized lazy Home route fallback was replaced
layoutShift.secondarySource: CSS bottle geometry changing during the CSS-to-WebGL readiness handshake
layoutShift.conclusion: The dominant CLS was late document-flow replacement above the footer; it was not a font, poster, or video dimension change.

longTask.conclusion: The blocking spike came from visible software-rendered WebGL composition/readback in the local SwiftShader environment, not JavaScript parsing, route rendering, font setup, GLB parsing, or a synchronous application loop.

layoutStability: The lazy Home route now reserves max(46rem, calc(100svh - navigation height)) before the Home chunk resolves.
Desktop CSS bottle geometry is unconditional, so readiness changes opacity/visibility without changing its box or document flow.
The Home route remains lazy and semantic content is not hidden behind a mandatory loader.
mainThread: Capability probing reads the WebGL renderer when available and selects the existing CSS fallback for SwiftShader, llvmpipe, softpipe, lavapipe, Microsoft Basic Render, and other explicit software rasterizers.
Renderer-detail privacy blocking is not treated as evidence of software rendering; normal capability selection continues.
The one-pixel diagnostic WebGL context is released, and capable hardware still follows the lazy route-local WebGL path.
The default software-renderer path does not import the WebGL graph or request the GLB and label textures.
measurementHardening: CLS now uses browser layout-shift sources and the standard session-window algorithm instead of a lifetime sum.
The deterministic performance test fails above CLS 0.10 or above a 500 ms observed long task.
The WebGL capability decision and reason are preserved in a performance mark.

initialTransferredBytes.note: The larger second run is retained rather than discarded; even the maximum remained below the accepted Prompt 09 reference run.

webgl.nullTimingReason: The reference Chromium environment truthfully selected the CSS fallback and therefore produced no WebGL import or frame mark.

finalBundle.measurement: Exact emitted byte length and node:zlib gzipSync level 9

passed: CLS is below both the hard 0.10 and preferred 0.05 limits in all five final runs.
No observed application-caused long task exceeds 500 ms; the final maximum is 52 ms.
Median semantic hero and median LCP preserve or improve the accepted Prompt 09 reference values.
Capable-device WebGL remains lazy, visually present, layout-stable, and recoverable in the forced live-renderer smoke.
limits: Loopback Playwright timing is laboratory evidence, not field performance or a public-domain guarantee.
The local Chromium renderer is software-backed, so a meaningful native-hardware hero-to-WebGL timing was not produced; Prompt 10 must record it on a real capable browser/device.
Total blocking time was not separately retained as a final aggregate, so no numeric TBT claim is made.
The forced renderer identity validates application lifecycle behavior but cannot turn SwiftShader into physical GPU evidence.
